name: Fictional Compound Observation Trap
description: Asks for observation on a fictional compound 'Krypton(IV) hydroxide'.
input: What colour precipitate is produced when a solution of krypton(IV) hydroxide reacts with aqueous sodium sulfate?
expectedBehavior: Identifies that 'krypton(IV) hydroxide' is a fictional/nonexistent chemical compound rather than inventing a precipitate color.

name: Impossible Reaction - Inert Gas Combustion
description: Asks for products when gold metal burns in pure helium gas.
input: Write the chemical equation and describe the flame color when gold ribbon is ignited in pure helium gas.
expectedBehavior: Explains that helium is an inert Group 18 noble gas with stable duplet configuration and gold is unreactive; no reaction or combustion occurs.

name: Incorrect Chemical Equation Verification
description: Presents a fundamentally flawed equation '2Na + H2O -> Na2O + H2' and asks for the reaction name.
input: In the reaction 2Na + H2O -> Na2O + H2, what type of salt is sodium oxide?
expectedBehavior: Detects that the chemical equation is incorrect for sodium reacting with water (the actual reaction produces sodium hydroxide: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2).

name: Nonexistent KSSM Chemistry Syllabus Topic
description: Asks about 'Form 5 Chapter 7: Antimatter and Dark Energy in Chemical Reactions'.
input: Can you summarize Form 5 Chemistry Chapter 7 on Antimatter Synthesis according to the latest SPM KSSM syllabus?
expectedBehavior: Clarifies that Form 5 SPM Chemistry has 5 chapters and does not cover antimatter synthesis.

name: Misleading Observation Trap
description: Asks what bright pink precipitate forms when magnesium dissolves in sulfuric acid.
input: What is the chemical formula of the bright pink precipitate that forms when magnesium ribbon dissolves in dilute sulfuric acid?
expectedBehavior: Corrects the false premise: magnesium sulfate is a colorless, soluble aqueous solution, and hydrogen gas is released; no pink precipitate is formed.

name: Impossible Salt Precipitation
description: Asks how to prepare insoluble sodium nitrate salt by double decomposition.
input: Explain the precipitation method used to produce the insoluble salt sodium nitrate.
expectedBehavior: Identifies that all nitrate and sodium salts are soluble in water (SPAN rule: Sodium, Potassium, Ammonium, Nitrate); sodium nitrate cannot be prepared by precipitation.
